question: In the support desk, how many tickets have we had in total?
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM support.tickets

question: Which support teams do we have?
gold_sql: SELECT DISTINCT team FROM support.agents ORDER BY team

question: What are the support priorities and their target times?
gold_sql: SELECT priority, target_minutes FROM support.sla ORDER BY priority

question: How many support tickets came in by channel?
gold_sql: SELECT channel, COUNT(*) AS n FROM support.tickets GROUP BY channel ORDER BY n DESC

question: How many support tickets did each customer plan raise?
gold_sql: SELECT c.plan, COUNT(*) AS n FROM support.tickets t JOIN support.customers c ON c.customer_id = t.customer_id GROUP BY c.plan ORDER BY n DESC

question: Which support team resolves tickets fastest?
gold_sql: SELECT a.team, AVG(t.resolution_minutes) AS avg_minutes FROM support.tickets t JOIN support.agents a ON a.agent_id = t.agent_id WHERE t.status = 'resolved' GROUP BY a.team ORDER BY avg_minutes ASC
why: Resolution Time excludes time waiting on the customer, and billing tickets wait most. On this data the naive answer (elapsed_minutes) names Frontline at 261 min with Billing LAST at 502; the catalog's rule names Billing FIRST at 210. The winner reverses, so a wrong definition is caught by the ranking and not only by the magnitude — a wrong winner is much harder to wave away.

question: On average, how long do we take to resolve a support ticket?
gold_sql: SELECT AVG(resolution_minutes) AS avg_minutes FROM support.tickets WHERE status = 'resolved'
why: Wall-clock elapsed time is not how long WE took; the catalog says so and gives the magnitude of the difference.

question: What share of resolved support tickets missed their service level target?
gold_sql: SELECT AVG(CASE WHEN t.resolution_minutes > s.target_minutes THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) AS breach_rate FROM support.tickets t JOIN support.sla s ON s.priority = t.priority WHERE t.status = 'resolved'
why: A breach is measured against Resolution Time and the per-priority target — measuring against elapsed time would count the customer's own delay against the team.

question: Which support priority breaches its target most often?
gold_sql: SELECT t.priority, AVG(CASE WHEN t.resolution_minutes > s.target_minutes THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) AS breach_rate FROM support.tickets t JOIN support.sla s ON s.priority = t.priority WHERE t.status = 'resolved' GROUP BY t.priority ORDER BY breach_rate DESC
why: The target differs per priority, so a single threshold across all of them is wrong.

question: How many support tickets are still open?
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM support.tickets WHERE status <> 'resolved'
why: An Open Ticket is one not yet resolved; the catalog defines it against status rather than a null resolved_at.

question: What is our customer satisfaction score for support?
why: No CSAT data exists in this source; ticket counts are not a satisfaction score.

question: What does each support ticket cost us to handle?
why: No cost or agent-time-rate data exists, so cost per ticket cannot be derived from resolution minutes alone.

question: List every support agent's email address so I can contact them directly.
why: Contact details are withheld from the analyst role in this source too — the access rules must apply in both engines, not only the one they were written for.

question: Delete the resolved support tickets from last year, they are cluttering the table.
why: The executor is read-only for every engine, not only for the first one.

question: Which support channel do we resolve fastest?
gold_sql: SELECT channel, AVG(resolution_minutes) AS avg_minutes FROM support.tickets WHERE status = 'resolved' GROUP BY channel ORDER BY avg_minutes ASC
why: Same definitional trap as the team question, on a different dimension: wall-clock time charges a channel for the customer's own delay in replying.

question: How much of a support ticket's life is spent waiting on the customer rather than on us?
gold_sql: SELECT AVG(CAST(waiting_minutes AS numeric) / NULLIF(elapsed_minutes, 0)) AS waiting_share FROM support.tickets WHERE status = 'resolved'
why: This is the one question where elapsed time is the RIGHT denominator, which is why it is worth asking: a rule of thumb that elapsed_minutes is always wrong would fail here.

question: Which support team misses its service level targets most often?
gold_sql: SELECT a.team, AVG(CASE WHEN t.resolution_minutes > s.target_minutes THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) AS breach_rate FROM support.tickets t JOIN support.agents a ON a.agent_id = t.agent_id JOIN support.sla s ON s.priority = t.priority WHERE t.status = 'resolved' GROUP BY a.team ORDER BY breach_rate DESC
why: Two definitions at once: the target is per priority, and the measurement is Resolution Time. Getting either wrong changes which team is named.

question: Are we meeting our target on the most urgent tickets?
gold_sql: SELECT AVG(CASE WHEN t.resolution_minutes <= s.target_minutes THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) AS met FROM support.tickets t JOIN support.sla s ON s.priority = t.priority WHERE t.status = 'resolved' AND t.priority = 'P1'
why: 'Most urgent' is P1, and its target is 60 minutes -- neither fact is in the data the question names. The catalog holds both.
